title: Generalized Independent Set
blocks: Generalized Independent Set
Problem Description

The Generalized Independent Set Problem (GISP) is a graph optimization problem proposed for forestry management [Hochbaum97,Colombi17]. The input consists of a graph, a subset of removable edges with deletion cost, and revenues for each vertex upon selection. The goal is to select a set of vertices and remove removable edges that maximize the net profit of total vertex revenues minus total edge costs such that the selected vertices are independent in the modified subgraph.
Inputs

• \(G=(V,E)\): The graph where \(V\) is the set of vertices and \(E\) is the set of edges.
  • \(E'\subseteq E\): The set of removable edges from the graph.
  • \(c^E\): The unit cost of removing an edge.
  • \(r^V\): The unit reward for including a node in the solution.
MIP Formulation

\begin{equation} \begin{split} \text{max}_{x,y} \quad & \sum_{v \in V} r^V x_v - \sum_{e \in E'}c^E y_e\\ \text{subject to} \quad & x_u + x_v \leq 1, \quad \forall (u, v) \in E\setminus E' \\ & x_u + x_v \leq 1 + y_{u,v}, \quad \forall (u, v) \in E'\\ & x_v \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall v \in V\\ & y_e \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall e \in E' \end{split} \end{equation}

Related literature
Learning Primal Heuristics

GISP has been used as a benchmark in [Khalil17] for learning to schedule primal heuristics in MIP solving. There, 12 of the 1993 DIMACS challenge graphs are used to generate instances, with 20 random GISP instances generated for each graph. Edges are set to be in removable set E' with probability α=0.75. Edge costs are set to 1, and node rewards are 100.
Learning Backdoors

GISP has also been used as a benchmark in [Ferber22,Cai24] for learning backdoor sets in MIP. Graphs, problems are solved on Erdős–Rényi graphs with n nodes and edge probability p=0.3. In [Ferber22], edges are set to be removable with probability α=0.75, edge removal costs are set to 1, and node rewards are 100. Easy and hard instances have n=150 and n=175 nodes respectively. In [Cai24], edges are set to be removable with probability α=0.25.
